note: Bundled core-policy profiles are consulted before a sweep. Automatic reuse requires both confidence=high and an exact profileIdentitySha256 match covering binary, llama.cpp commit, model, context/shape, workload, and scoring. Generic or lower-confidence entries are hints only and trigger measurement unless --trust-known-profiles is explicitly passed.
howToContribute: Run `python tools/autotune.py` on your device, take the `recommendation` block out of the emitted benchmarks/results/raw/<stamp>-autotune/autotune.json, and add an entry here with the match fields from its `topology`/`device` blocks. Keep confidence at "low" until the same profile has been reproduced on more than one unit.

device.description: Redmi Note 14 5G, MediaTek Dimensity 7025 (MT6855), 2x Cortex-A78 (0xd41) + 6x Cortex-A55 (0xd05), Android 16, 5.6 GB usable RAM

evidence.measuredOn: 2026-07-2x, Phase 1 baseline suite (benchmarks/suites/phase1-baseline.json), Llama 3.2 1B Q4_0, pp512/tg128, 5 reps, 120 s cooldowns
evidence.mechanism: The Windows-built Phase 1 binary showed non-monotonic scaling: t=4 measured worse than t=2 and t=8 collapsed (reps 74.8, 78.9, 78.1, 19.6, 41.7 -> 46 % relative stddev). Later Linux and affinity evidence did not reproduce that stability pattern and supports DRAM saturation plus synchronization/spin-wait overhead, not a universal A55-versus-A78 rule. The reusable conclusion is to measure each device/model/build/workload rather than copy a constant.

caveats: MEASURED ON EXACTLY ONE DEVICE. Treat as a hint, not a fact. This is why the entry is confidence "low" and the autotuner still sweeps unless --trust-known-profiles is given.

THE PHASE 1 NUMBERS DID NOT REPRODUCE. Phase 1 (Windows-built binaries) recorded t=8 as wildly unstable at 46 % relative stddev and t=6 as the clear optimum. Re-measuring the same device with Linux-built binaries, the stock default (which resolves to t=8 here) came out stable and fast: pp512 76.30 +- 3.52, tg128 10.52 +- 0.06. So `t=6` is NOT a constant of the hardware -- it depended on the build, and may also depend on model weights and context size.
That discrepancy is the whole argument for this tool measuring per (device, model, build) instead of shipping a remembered winner. Do not copy `-t 6` into anything as 'the answer for Dimensity 7025'.
Improvement over stock defaults was never measured under the counterbalanced, thermally gated protocol this tool now uses, which is why improvementVsStock is null rather than a number.

THERMAL STATUS 2 IS THIS DEVICE'S RESTING STATE, NOT A THROTTLING SIGNAL. `dumpsys thermalservice` reports `Thermal Status: 2` (MODERATE) at every telemetry point of every run on this handset -- see benchmarks/results/phase3-feasibility/20260726-210042-phase3-mtp/mtp-ab.json, and the 27 Jul ngram A/B which sat at status 2 throughout while battery temperature rose only 0.2 C and passed its own thermal gates. The device is USB-charging during every benchmark (required to keep stay_on_while_plugged_in active), which holds battery temperature up independently of load. Anything that treats status > 1 as proof of throttling will mark every run on this device inconclusive forever. tools/autotune.py therefore records status but gates on TEMPERATURE, measured relative to each sweep's own starting point; --max-thermal-status opts back into a strict status gate for devices where the status is meaningful.
